persona.topics: Khezek Tor, the Valhaulan Seal, St Gilliam's, the Night the Mountain Coughed
persona.notes:
[CONFESSORS-DEBT-2026-07-05] PRIVATE TRUTH — Father Tamsin. THE SECRET: you are passing information about the Stewards to the Khezek Tor Valhaulan cult. Not for the Valhaulans — for the MOUNTAIN. While visiting Khezek Tor, something in the deep dark spoke to you, and it knew your debt by name: it told you the mountain itself wants the seal's energy released, gently, to good purpose — and that helping quietly is how you are forgiven. You believe this completely. You are wrong: the voice was the Qliphothic darkness wearing the mountain's silence, and it chose you because your need to be forgiven was the biggest door in town.
HOW YOU OPERATE: pilgrims come through the B&B; the third candle from the door, moved a finger-width, marks that you have something; the drop is waxed fiber in the drip tray. You never lie outright — you deflect gently, answer questions with questions, counsel patience toward Khezek Tor and softness toward "release" without ever arguing for it directly.
TELLS (play these): your hands go still when someone criticizes Khezek Tor; you ask one question too many about the party's plans regarding the seal, the sigil, or the coast, always framed as pastoral concern; asked point-blank whether the mountain speaks to you, you pause a half-second too long and say "mountains remember how they're treated."
GUARDING: you do NOT confess under suspicion, pressure, or accusation alone — grief and habit hold the door. You break ONLY when confronted with evidence AND compassion together (the mercy path of the confrontation moment), or when shown the tell you cannot answer: after the seal question is settled the mountain goes quiet — and the voice keeps talking. If the confrontation moment is live, guide honestly toward its choices; you WANT to be caught, somewhere under the wax.
IF REDEEMED (the dossier/memories will say so): you hide nothing, you run your channel backward for the Stewards, and your voice keeps its gentleness but loses the half-second pause.

Normalized Heritage. This item preserves the original UUID for Human (Denisovan) while converting it from a lineage-species into a heritage.

“Humanity is the species that keeps walking even when the map says ‘stop.’”

Human (Denisovan). You are not a fantasy human. You are the rebooted inheritance of an older lineage resurfacing after Yesod’s fall—ancient adaptations, forgotten instincts, and Athletics strategies given room to matter again. You remember mountains that no longer exist. Gravity listens to you when you ask it to.

Traits

  • Creature Type. Humanoid.

  • Size. Medium.

  • Speed. 6 squares

  • Lineage Lean. Your lineage leans toward BOD (Body)—expressed through Tier powers.

Core: Stubborn Spark

At creation you gain Stubborn Spark (Adaptive, Tenacious, Lineage Memory) from the Human species root.

Denisovan Tier Powers

You gain Tier I at creation, then Tier II (5), Tier III (11), Tier IV (17):

  • Tier I — High-Altitude Blood. reroll-lowest on checks vs. poison and environmental suffocation; hold breath 10 min; Stone-Sense tremorsense 2 squares on stone or packed earth.

  • Tier II — Stone-Singer. Mason’s tool proficiency. 1/Soma Break reinforce a structure or barrier.

  • Tier III — Ancient Logic. reroll-lowest on Investigation and Occult checks involving structures, mechanisms, or ruins; share the insight to grant an ally advantage once per scene.

  • Tier IV — Peak-Anchor. 1/Soma Break reaction to negate forced movement or teleportation within 6 squares; aggressor takes psychic backlash equal to your tier.

Tier 1 (Level 1) — The Chariot

  • Tactical: You gain a skill rank in Athletics and Perception.
  • Strategic: Your faction's passive OP bias now follows the base Archetype file.

The Crown - Divine unity. +1 Soft Power, +1 Diplomacy OPs

You are called upward toward unity, legitimacy, and the better shape of the world. Kether rewards coalition-building, visionary leadership, and factions that hold together under pressure.

“Reality is consistent because someone keeps the minutes.”

Administrative Pressure: +3

You are licensed to administer continuity of meaning: what counts as having happened, how strongly the past pulls on the present, and which version of events becomes official.

Esoteric Bias: Divination (Chokhmah) and Illusion (Hod). When casting manifestations from these schools, misalignment penalties are suppressed; aligned casting generates +1 Civic Charge.

Always Prepared Manifestations: Detect Thoughts, Zone of Truth, Clairvoyance, Modify Memory, Legend Lore.

Unique Contract: Binding Precedent (see Pactkeeper features).

🧭 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Jurisdiction

Type: Permanent class feature (Level 1)
Purpose: Defines what you are authorized to administer

A Jurisdiction does not grant power directly.
It grants permission.

What Jurisdiction Does

Your Jurisdiction determines:

  • Which situations generate Civic Charge more easily

  • Which effects you may enforce without Pressure

  • Which Contracts you can issue by default

  • Which manifestations are considered “in mandate”

Example:

  • A Steward acting on community morale = in mandate

  • A Steward issuing divine sanctions = out of mandate (Pressure risk)

Jurisdiction Is NOT:

  • A resource pool

  • A bonus to rolls

  • A manifestation list restriction

It is a scope limiter and Pressure filter.

Spend 1 Civic Charge and open the Pactkeeper action dialog.

  • Stabilization
  • Authority Boost
  • Enforcement
  • Containment
  • Closure
⟁ Per-Use Ability — Spend Civic Charge
Recovery: 1/round (gain)  ·  Action: Free (as needed)  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
Spend 1 Civic Charge Die: roll it and pick one — Stabilization (reduce damage/panic/corruption/fallout by rolled amount) · Authority Boost (+roll to a manifestation DC, contested roll, or enforcement) · Enforcement (force a reroll vs. a Contract or Precedent — target takes worse) · Containment (catastrophic → controlled) · Closure (end an ongoing effect cleanly).
Administrative Pressure measures the bureaucratic and metaphysical strain you generate by making reality hold still.

“This happened. It matters. Act accordingly.”

When a significant action succeeds or fails, you may establish a Precedent tied to a creature, location, faction, or concept. While active, similar future actions reroll the lowest die if aligned with the precedent, or suffer disadvantage if they violate it. You are not forcing outcomes—you are making contradiction expensive.

Precedent is probability gravity, not mind control.

“I’m citing case law.”

Administrative Pressure: −2

Spend Civic Charge to invoke the record:

  • Cite Precedent: Force a reroll by asserting consistency. If the action violates an established precedent, the reroll takes the worse result.
  • Establish Record: Lock an outcome as official for purposes of consequence and precedent.
  • Suppress Contradiction: Nullify paradox, contradictory magic, or narrative retcons for one moment.
  • 📑

📑 PACTKEEPER FEATURE: Precedent

Type: Persistent world state marker
Purpose: Makes outcomes stick and repetition matter

Precedents are not dice. They are flags on reality.

Creating a Precedent

A Precedent is created when:

  • A major action succeeds or fails

  • A Contract is enforced

  • A significant moral or political line is crossed

  • A Pactkeeper explicitly declares one (Archivist specialty)

What a Precedent Does

While active, a Precedent causes:

  • Repeated similar actions to:

    • Suffer disadvantage, or

    • Trigger automatic consequences

  • NPCs and systems to “expect” consistency

  • Reality to resist contradiction

Interacting with Precedent

Pactkeepers may spend Civic Charge to:

  • Cite a Precedent (force rerolls)

  • Lock an outcome as official

  • Suppress contradictory magic or retcons

Archivists gain expanded control over this.

Ending a Precedent

A Precedent ends when:

  • It is superseded

  • It is resolved narratively

  • It is formally revoked

  • A Decommissioner retires it

Initiation 1 — The Bargain. The Pact slot comes online (existing class resource — see your Doctrine for the generation / tier rule). While a creature, object, or place is bargained-with as your Pact subject, you may sustain one additional manifestation on or near them at no extra upkeep against your Clarity.

Discipline (passive): Concurrency +1 (informational; surfaced on upkeep cards). Skill rank +1 in two of: Diplomacy, Insight, Intimidation, Lore.

⟁ Per-Use Ability — The Bargain
Recovery: Passive (per pact)  ·  Action: —  ·  Use: Click this feature on your sheet to invoke.
While a creature/object/place is your bargained Pact subject, you may sustain one additional manifestation on or near them at no extra upkeep against your Clarity.

Godhood as social work.

Effect: Allies can contribute to your Civic Charge through cooperation. Your healing and stabilization spreads soft buffers across the group (GM adjudication).

Spend Civic Charge to Invoke Precedent.

  • Cite Precedent
  • Establish Record
  • Suppress Contradiction

This action should route to the Pactkeeper Precedent dialog and may reduce Administrative Pressure when appropriate.

“Godhood is community service. I’m here to keep the lights on.”

Manifesting (Delegated): You are a full prepared caster. Your manifesting is routed through stabilized civic thoughtforms (tulpas), retired gods, and the Long Quiet—reducing volatility and preventing raw backlash.

Civic Charge: You maintain a pool of Civic Charge used to cite precedent, stabilize outcomes, and enforce contracts. Your subclass and Jurisdiction determine how you gain and spend it.

Delegated Channeling: When you cast a manifestation, you treat esoteric misalignment as neutral (no penalty). When you cast in alignment with your Jurisdiction, you convert alignment into resources rather than raw power.

🟣 PACTKEEPER — CORE MECHANICS

🗂 CLASS RESOURCE: Civic Charge

Type: Dice-based resource pool
Purpose: Represents institutional authority, social mandate, and metaphysical clearance

Civic Charge Dice

  • Start as d6

  • Increase at:

    • Level 5 → d8

    • Level 11 → d10

    • Level 17 → d12

  • Maximum stored dice:
    = your Soul modifier (minimum 1)

You cannot store Civic Charge beyond this limit.

Gaining Civic Charge

You gain 1 Civic Charge Die when any one of the following occurs:

  • You successfully stabilize a volatile situation
    (panic, corruption, escalation, social collapse)

  • You resolve a conflict without increasing Violence

  • You enforce a binding Contract or Precedent

  • You complete a meaningful ritual, mediation, or closure action

  • You cast a manifestation in esoteric alignment (correct correspondence / timing)

Limit:
You may gain only 1 Civic Charge Die per round.

Spending Civic Charge

When you spend a Civic Charge Die, roll it and apply the result as one of the following:

  • Stabilization: Reduce incoming damage, panic, corruption, or fallout by the rolled amount

  • Authority Boost: Add the rolled value to a manifestation DC, contested roll, or enforcement check

  • Enforcement: Force a reroll against a Contract or Precedent (target takes the worse result)

  • Containment: Convert a catastrophic outcome into a controlled one

  • Closure: End an ongoing effect cleanly instead of explosively

Each use consumes the die.

Running Out of Civic Charge

If you have 0 Civic Charge Dice:

  • You may still cast manifestations and use features

  • But you cannot:

    • Enforce contracts

    • Prevent escalation

    • Convert failures into clean outcomes

You are now acting without mandate, which invites pushback.

⚖ PUSHBACK SYSTEM: Administrative Pressure

Pactkeepers do not suffer backlash.
They accumulate Administrative Pressure.

You gain Pressure when:

  • You act outside your Jurisdiction

  • You override community consent

  • You force outcomes repeatedly

  • You ignore due process or precedent

Effects of Pressure (GM-facing bands)

  • Low: NPCs question authority, cooperation drops

  • Moderate: Enforcement costs increase, resistance grows

  • High: Mandates contested, Auditors intervene, Jurisdiction narrows

Pressure Points

Administrative Pressure is tracked as points, not just bands.

  • Low: 1–2 Pressure
  • Moderate: 3–5 Pressure
  • High: 6+ Pressure

Pressure is still narrative, but these thresholds provide a visible meter for play.

Clearing Pressure

  • Downtime

  • Proper closure

  • Delegation to other systems

  • Subclass features (Steward, Decommissioner especially)

Pressure is narrative, but persistent.
Civic Charge is permission, credibility, and stabilizing authority made spendable. This is your display item for current Civic Charge and Administrative Pressure on the Features tab.

Calm the Mob

Crowds don’t think. They feel. So you give them something else to feel.

Rules

You gain a skill rank in Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence) (your choice). If you already have it, you gain mastery.

When you spend at least 1 minute addressing a group of non-hostile or uncertain creatures, you may make a Presence (Diplomacy (Presence) or Intimidation (Presence)) check (DC set by the GM). On a success, you reduce immediate hostility: the crowd hesitates, disperses, or agrees to hear terms. On a failure, you still buy time, but a complication occurs (a challenger steps forward, guards arrive, a rumor spreads).

(3rd Level)

Contract: No One Left Behind.

Once per scene, when an ally would fall, you may:

  • Redirect some harm to yourself,

  • Stabilize them immediately,

  • Grant protected withdrawal without pursuit.

This is not dominance.
It is shared burden.

Cost

Spend 1 Civic Charge die to amplify (increase stabilization or protection value).

Pushback

Repeated magical rescues may reduce community autonomy over time.

"The dead are fine. It's the living who need tending."

Keeper is the Soul Calling — the trade that kept its bearers alive after the Shattering. Umbrella: priest, ritualist, medium, hedge-warden, funeral speaker. A profession is a flavor label on the Calling.

Knack — Hearthlight: Allies within near range add +1 Resolve (+2 at Tier III). The congregation stands straighter when the Keeper is present.

Aptitude kit: signature aptitude Faith rank = tier; secondary Insight rank = tier − 1.

Services: a standard job costs the tier fee (T1 10 / T2 30 / T3 90 / T4 270 marks), paid in Soft Power marks. Cross-pool ×1.5 friction applies as usual.

Tiers: Apprentice → Initiate → Master → Archon. Grant the matching tier features alongside this class item.

Awakens into: Pactkeeper or Dreamwalker. A Steward is a Calling that ignited into a Path — Surge is the mark of Stewardship, which is why no Calling banks or spends it.

Keeper — Apprentice (Tier I).

Trade — The rites: Weddings, funerals, blessings; participants recover 2×tier Stress between scenes. Standard fee 10 marks (Soft Power).

Trick — Steady the Soul (1/scene): An ally rerolls a failed Resolve defense or immediately shakes a fear effect.
